text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Four of Australia's big banks - the National Australia Bank, Commonwealth Bank of Australia, ANZ Banking Group and the Colonial State Bank - have joined forces to create BankPay in an attempt to dominate Australia's A$300 billion-a-year market in third party electronic bill payments. BankPay, to be launched in May, will amalgamate the individual bank paying facilities offered by each of the banks. Page 1.

Studies being undertaken at the Brain Services Institute in Melbourne aim to objectively measure the brain's activity in response to smell, which accounts for about 70 per cent of the taste sensation. The world's food and fragrance industries would seek he results to allow market researchers to target potential customers. Page 3.

NSW electricity distributor Integral Energy has secured large contracts with Telstra, the Commonwealth Bank and Westfield Holdings, gaining a big victory in the newly regulated State power market. This confirms the move to a national electricity market wll be a ruthless battle for large clients and will threaten the survival of the smaller players. Page 17.

It is expected to be the best winter for retailers in years, following strong sales over the Easter break and early cool weather in some States. While there is caution against predicting a strong sustained upturn, food sales have been firm and apparel, manchester and brown goods sales are improving. Page 17.

Optus Communications has pulled off a good deal by convincing its partners to leave the Optus Vision cable business, but it must do better to strike a bigger deal with Telstra. Deals will be done over the next few months as both sides prepare for public loats. Page 19.

BHP will implement major cost-cutting measures, including major job cuts at some North American copper assets, to obtain profits from its A$3.2 billion Magnma Copper acquisition. There has been a series of poor results from the Magma assets since BHP acqired it in late 1995. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

The National Australia Bank is tipped to be the narrow front-runner in a closely fought fight between five groups, including the ANZ Bank, to gain the management rights to the New South Wales Government's funds management business, Axiom, and has offered to move its funds management operations to Sydney to ensure it wins the A$200 million bidding war. Page 19.

Coca-Cola Amatil, the Australian bottler that controls CCA Indonesia, is planning huge growth in the Indonesian soft drinks market, announcing it has committed millions of dollars to new production facilities and cool units for its 400,000 retailers and agressive advertising campaigns. CCA's Jakarta-based regional director John Brady says the company hasn't even scratched the surface yet, but it is possible a decade from now, Indonesia may generate more than A$3 billion in sales for the Australian firm. Pge 19.

After expanding into Vietnam and China, Philippines-based brewing and packaging group San Miguel is believed to be conducting talks with the South Australian and Victorian Governments about a possible bottle making plant as part of the company's plans to reak ACI's monopoly on the manufacture of Australian wine bottles. Page 21.

According to the latest report by Tony Hodgson, of Ferrier Hodgson - the liquidator of the three former Farrow Group building societies, Pyramid, Geelong and Countrywide - the estimated dividend payable to shareholders in the former Pyramid Building Sociey has dropped from 49 cents in the dollar to 44-45 cents because of the inclusion of about 10,000 non-withdrawing investing shareholders. Page 21.

Canada-listed Calliope Metals Corp has lodged a prospectus with the Australian Securities Commission to raise A$10.5 million and is preparing to list on the Australian Stock Exchange as part of its plan to build a A$300 million nickel and cobalt refinery to Gladstone in Queensland. Page 21,

Prime Minister John Howard announced yesterday that Federal Government-owned investment house AIDC Ltd has signed its second water infrastructure contract in China. The project follows a A$33 million water contract last year and will involve the constructon of an A$18 million treatment plant in the city of Shaoxing on the Yangtze River delta. Page 21.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

As part of an ambitious plan to build an international health care business centred in Europe, Mayne Nickless, already Australia's biggest private hospital operator with 36 hospitals in five States, is believed to have bid about A$1 billion for Europe's largest hospital operator, Generale de Sante, and expects to know by the weekend whether the bid was successful. Page 25.

According to a memo obtained by the Herald, FAI Insurances chief executive Rodney Adler says the company is close to signing a joint-venture agreement with California-based Liberty Mutual - one of the largest workers compensation insurers in the United States - to manage its workers compensation division - a deal Adler says will be tedious but beneficial to both parties. Page 25.

Amid indications Telstra and Optus may soon move to share their high-capacity cable networks in a bid to reduce costs, Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chief Allan Fels has revealed in an interview any Telstra-Optus infrastructure deal is liely to require investigation and approval by the ACCC. Page 27.

Australian traders were yesterday hoping for a rebound from the two per cent loss on the US sharemarket last week as they anxiously await the outcome of today's key Reserve Bank board meeting, the upcoming decision on the ACTU's call for a A$20 safety netpay rise for workers who have not received a pay rise under enterprise bargaining, and the release of the Wallis report into the financial system. Page 27.

A group of borrowers from the Western Australian-based Challenge Bank has successfully applied to have a bankruptcy notice issued early this year by Westpac Banking Corporation, which bought Challenge in September 1995, set aside after the Federal Court ruled Westpac had failed to amend the record of the Supreme Court as required. Page 27.

Following a move by United States investment bank Merrill Lynch to downgrade Amcor's profit earnings estimates amid fears of an increase in US interest rates and higher inventories in January for many pulp and paper products, Amcor's hopes of a strong profit performance in the second half of this year have suffered a setback. Page 27.
THE AGE

In an interview with The Age, Australian Competition and Consumer Commission chief Allan Fels said infrastructure sharing between Optus and Telstra could have "far reaching effects on competition and effective resource allocation" and he said such deals are potentially the Commission's toughest challenge of the next few years. Page B1.

According to a memo dated March 7, FAI Insurances looks set to finalise a joint venture, to be consummated by September 30, with giant United States workers' compensation insurer Liberty Mutual, which has a portfolio worth over A$2.5 billion, to manage it workers' compensation division. Page B1.

Tony Barlow Australia has sold off its Shearer's division to a company associated with the Melbourne-based Stafford Group for A$1.95 million. The deal was announced following the Supreme Court's criticism of TBA for withholding financial information fromits shareholders. Page B1.

The AMP is holding talks with fund management companies in Britain and the United States that it may consider buying. A spokesman would not confirm or deny reports that AMP was considering a A$4.1 billion offer for the UK-based National Provident Institution. Page B1.

Financial markets are expected to fall after the release of various United States data has increased the likelihood of a rise in US interest rates. Australian analysts also predict local sharemarkets will follow the US trends. Page B1.

Amcor's expectations of a profit rise in the second half of 1997 have been lowered with an analyst predicting that high inventories and soft demand will delay a recovery in pulp and paper price. Stockbroker Merrill Lynch also forecasts that prices of fine paper will not recover until next year. Page B2.
